text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran pprof on host ingress while replaying streaming requests. seeing a big host-side CPU bump for long streams (>~512 tokens). flame points at tokenization + request parse path and lots of small writev syscalls. link to flame: https://internal.perf/1705/ingress-flame (private)
lin: can you paste the hot stacks / top symbols?

maria: top stacks pasted below (trimmed):
```
parse::stream_frame -> parse::tokenize_input -> std::string::append -> malloc / memcpy
grpc::writev_wrap -> multiple writev calls per chunk -> syscall
kvcache::lookup -> vector rehash on hot path (observed spikes)
```
numbers: baseline host CPU ~12% during normal short requests; for long streaming runs host CPU climbs to ~72%. per-token host overhead increases from ~1.9ms -> ~5.7ms (avg across traces).

ryan: oof. looks like a mix: (1) allocator churn from tokenization creating new strings, (2) parse/deserialize copies frames into new buffers, (3) HTTP/gRPC framing producing many small writev ops. any IO batching disabled?

maria: confirmed — we still do a parse -> reserialize step for header/frame assembly before handing to runtime. and tokenizer returns std::string per token slice which forces allocations on many workloads. grpc side: we call SendMsg for each chunk and kernel coalescing is limited by how the grpc layer builds iovec.

perf-bot: summary (automated): avg CPU delta +60% on host for long stream load. 52% of host cycles attributed to memcpy/alloc paths. writev call count per request increased from ~4 -> ~28.

sam: two quick mitigations we can try: reuse a preallocated byte buffer for parse/serialization (avoid copies), and change tokenizer API to emit string_view/byte-slices to avoid allocations. both pretty low-risk for canary.

lin: i'll instrument writev counts and the allocator hotspots (jemalloc stats) on canary nodes. can we get a small repro script to reproduce consistently?

maria: repro steps below (run on staging):
```
# stream a long prompt, forcing host-side tokenization + streaming chunking
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","stream":true,"input":"'$(python -c 'print("word "*2000)')'"}' \
  https://staging-api.redwood.internal/v1/generate/stream
```
expected: see many small packets and high host CPU in pprof.

devon: another angle — kernel selection overhead: are we computing the preferred kernel for every request/sequence length at runtime? if that's happening per-request it might add extra cycles when combined with parse costs.

maria: good call — i saw a short path in runtime that recomputes kernel heuristics when the sequence length crosses thresholds. that function is cheap in isolation but adds up across ~1000 parallel streams.

ryan: plan suggestion:
- short-term canary: pool parse buffers + switch tokenizer to zero-copy byte-slices for the streaming path (eng-runtime change)
- measure writev coalescing: add coalescer in grpc bridge to batch small iovecs into fewer syscalls
- medium: memoize kernel selection by sequence-length bucket to avoid repeated heuristics per request
- evaluate kvcache eviction behavior: the prefetch/lookup pattern is causing vector growth; add capacity reservation on lookups.

sam: i can open a small PR for buffer pooling + tokenizer API change (streaming-only). want to keep global API stable, so will gate behind a feature flag: enable_zero_copy_stream_tokenize.

lin: i'll add tracing to count writev per request and record jemalloc arena stats. will run on canary nodes after sam's patch.

perf-bot: note: previous mitigation (2019-ingress-chunking) reduced p99 latency but did not address alloc churn; new approach targets host CPU and syscall rate.

maria: agreed. action items:
- sam: PR for buffer pooling + zero-copy streaming tokenizer (ETA end of day)
- lin: writev + allocator instrumentation on canary (ETA EOD)
- ryan: prototype grpc iovec coalescer (spike)
- devon: add kernel-selection memoization ticket (assign after triage)

sam: acked, starting on PR. will include a small benchmark (micro-bench) comparing std::string vs string_view path.

ryan: once we have the canary metrics we should run a short A/B: feature flag ON vs OFF under a synthetic stream load and measure tokens/sec, host CPU, and writev counts.

maria: thanks team. i'll coordinate the A/B and collect pprof flares. please post links to PRs and canary dashboards here. :eyes:

lin: noted. initial instrumentation running on canary now. will report numbers in ~2h. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: monitoring rule created: alert if avg writev/request > 20 OR host tokenization CPU > 40% across canary nodes for 5m.
